findings.title: Second `self.downsize` silently overrides the first and breaks the 4-argument call form
findings.body: The PR adds `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` (line 145) is kept. In Ruby the later definition replaces the earlier one, so the original method is dead code. Any existing caller using `downsize(from, to, width, height)` now passes `height` as `opts`, and `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` / `opts[:allow_animation]` then raise on a String or silently ignore the height. The method is also now ambiguous for the two-argument-plus-options shape. Keep one signature, or give the new method a distinct name.

findings.title: Removal of `OptimizedImage.dimensions` and change of `optimize` signature is an unannounced API break
findings.body: The PR removes the public class method `self.dimensions(width, height)` and changes `self.optimize` from taking width/height to taking a pre-formatted dimensions string. Any other caller in the codebase or plugins that calls `OptimizedImage.dimensions` or `optimize` with width/height will now fail with NoMethodError or ArgumentError. Nothing in the diff updates or checks such callers.

findings.title: Animated GIF path receives an invalid '80%' size for gifsicle
findings.body: When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on and the tempfile path ends in `.GIF`, `OptimizedImage.downsize` dispatches to `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, which is not a valid WxH argument. `convert_with` returns false on the non-zero exit and the loop silently retries 5 times with the same failing command, then the oversized animated GIF is passed on unchanged. Animated images therefore never get reduced, and the wasted work is repeated for every upload.

findings.title: Downsize failures are ignored and the final size is never verified
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on failure, but the return value is discarded. The loop also stops after 5 attempts without checking whether the file is now under `max_image_size_kb`. If it is still too large, the code falls through to `Upload.create_for` with no explicit error about the reduction failing. Also, reducing by 80% of dimensions does not guarantee a size reduction of the required amount, so 5 attempts may not be enough for large images. The result is either an unhelpful later rejection or an oversized file stored silently.

findings.title: Remote download limit no longer follows the admin setting
findings.body: The URL-download size cap changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hard-coded `10.megabytes`. Remote downloads of any file type through the API can now be up to 10MB regardless of the configured limit. This is a silent policy change that is not tied to the downsizing feature, which only concerns images. Note that this also removes the bound that limited how much would be fetched for images that are then downsized.

findings.title: Client-side size check ignores per-type site settings for all uploads
findings.body: The check in `validateUploadedFile` now uses a fixed 10MB for every upload type, replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. Attachments larger than the configured `max_attachment_size_kb` now pass client validation and are sent to the server, which means the admin's limit is bypassed in the UI. Only images should have their limit relaxed, since the server now downsizes them. Attachments should keep using their own setting.

findings.title: 413 error message hard-codes 10 MB instead of the configured limit
findings.body: The 413 handler now always reports a 10 MB limit via `file_too_large`, even when the site has a different `max_image_size_kb` or attachment limit configured. The user is told a wrong maximum size, which is misleading. The previous code read the actual setting.
